title: Indian Intelligence Warns Two PoK Groups Plan to Breach LoC on September 20-21
detail: Indian intelligence agencies, cited in reporting published September 11, 2026, warned that two Pakistan-based organisations in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK) were planning marches intended to breach the Line of Control: the Jamiat Ahl-e-Sunnat Khuiratta, Kotli, led by chief organiser Zafar Iqbal Ghazi, was reported planning an attempt on September 20, and a separate group from Garhi Dupatta in Muzaffarabad district — reportedly backed by local trade associations and private-school panels — was reported planning a follow-up attempt on September 21. The warning followed an earlier, similar march by JKLF activists toward the LoC that was dispersed by Pakistani authorities at Tatta Pani using cane-charging and tear gas, with some marchers responding with stone-pelting and several people arrested for property damage. The Indian Army said Pakistani army posts were 'instigating civilians to violate the LoC' and directed Indian forces to exercise restraint and, if required, fire only into the gaps rather than at crowds. As of publication, no breach attempt had occurred and it remained an intelligence warning rather than a confirmed incident.

media.caption: Indian intelligence warning on planned PoK marches to breach the Line of Control, September 11, 2026

confidenceReason: Single Indian outlet report attributed to unnamed intelligence agencies, describing a planned future action rather than a confirmed incident; no Pakistani government confirmation and no second independent outlet identified at time of writing.
